text:
maya: heads-up: ~30 GPU nodes in us-west1-g reporting NotReady. kubelet logs show device-plugin cert rotation errors, looks like CSR signing failing after KMS maintenance.

maya: logs: ```
I0318 13:07:12.123456    1234 deviceplugin.go:210] starting nvidia device plugin
E0318 13:07:12.123789    1234 cert.go:88] failed to load tls cert: x509: certificate signed by unknown authority
E0318 13:07:12.124000    1234 main.go:67] exiting: unable to obtain certificate: signing request denied
```

kevin: are the nvidia-driver daemonset pods healthy? or just the device-plugin?

maya: driver daemonset is Running on nodes, but device-plugin is CrashLoopBackOff across impacted nodes. ``kubectl get pods -n kube-system | grep nvidia`` shows many device-plugin pods in CrashLoopBackOff. kubelet on node shows plugin registration failing -> node gets tainted `nvidia.com/gpu-unavailable:NoSchedule`.

sasha: grim. cluster-autoscaler also reacted earlier and scaled down the preemptible GPU pool this morning (it thought workloads were low) — that made our buffer zero. We need immediate capacity and to stop autoscaler from removing any more GPU nodes until this is resolved.

infra-oncall: temporarily set annotation on the GPU nodepool to disable scale-down and increase min-size by +3. I'll patch CA config now. :eyes:

infra-oncall: ran: ```kubectl patch nodepool gpu-pool-usw1 -p '{"spec":{"autoscaling":{"minSize":6}}}' --type=merge```. Also added annotation `cluster-autoscaler.kubernetes.io/scale-down-disabled=true` to the nodepool config in the cloud console.

maya: trying a quick workaround: restart the cert-rotator sidecar and re-create device-plugin pods to trigger CSR re-request. Plan: `kubectl -n kube-system delete pod -l k8s-app=nvidia-device-plugin` then watch CSR status.

kevin: do we know why CSR signing failed? KMS key rotation was in progress earlier; could be HSM temporarily unreachable. Any KMS errors in cloud logs?

maya: yes, cloud KMS reported elevated error rates around 12:45 UTC due to control-plane upgrade. CSR approver rejected requests with `ca unavailable` message. Security flagged it as transient.

zack: heads-up about potential fallout: some training jobs will stay Pending because pods require GPUs and taints are NoSchedule. If we untaint before plugin healthy, pods will fail to see GPUs. We should keep taints until device-plugin confirms registration.

sasha: agree. steps: 1) stop scale-down (done). 2) restart cert-rotator/approver where possible. 3) force reissue device-plugin CSR by recreating pods. 4) once device-plugin reports `Registered` for each node, remove taint or uncordon.

maya: performed steps 2+3: restarted cert-approver deployment and deleted device-plugin pods. Watching CSR list: `kubectl get csr | grep nvidia` shows a bunch in `Pending`. Approver logs show intermittent `KMS signing timeout`.

ops-bot: Incident INC-2026-134 created (severity: S2) — assignees: infra-oncall, maya. Timeline doc: https://redwood.internal/incidents/INC-2026-134

infra-oncall: manual approve of a subset to get things rolling: `kubectl certificate approve nvidia-deviceplugin-req-...` for 10 nodes, device-plugin pods came up and registered on those nodes. :thumbsup:

maya: confirmed on those nodes: kubelet log `device plugin registered: nvidia.com/gpu` and node ready/gpu taint removed. Continuing to approve in batches to avoid flooding CA.

kevin: once stable, we should add a fallback path in cert rotator to retry with local CA when KMS is unavailable (or use cached signing cert) — file an engineering ticket.

sasha: also let's add a Cloudwatch/Prometheus alert for KMS signing latency linked to device-plugin CSR failures, and mark GPU nodepool as protected during KMS incidents.

zack: rollback plan if KMS remains down >1h: 1) deploy a pre-approved CA for device-plugin in cluster (short lived) 2) redeploy device-plugin to use that cert 3) alert security for manual rotation.

maya: current status at 14:40 UTC: 18/30 nodes recovered, device-plugin healthy on those. Patch to CA config applied. Continuing batch approvals.

infra-oncall: will keep autoscaler disabled for GPU pools until postmortem. I'll open follow-up: `ENGINFRA-725` for automation to prevent autoscaler scaling down when device-plugin CSR rate spikes.

kevin: thanks team. postmortem and followups please. :shipit:
